Consider the rectangular region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{4}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Which of the following could be the image of the left side of $Δ$ under the action of $T?$

choices.value: The image is the empty set

Consider the rectangular region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,3\le u\le 4,\,\,\frac{13\pi }{12}\le v\le \frac{13\pi }{9}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Which of the following could be the image of the left side of $Δ$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the left side.

For the left side, we have $u=3$ and $\frac{13\pi }{12}\le v\le \frac{13\pi }{9}.$ 

Substituting $u=3$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(3\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{13\pi }{12}\le v\le \frac{13\pi }{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is an equation of a circular arc of radius $3$ centered at the origin in the $xy$-plane. 
The arc lies in the third quadrant between the polar rays $\theta =\frac{13\pi }{12}$ and $\theta =\frac{13\pi }{9},$ as shown below.
